examples.en: This soup has lots of solid ingredients, so it's filling.
I fished out the solids and drank only the broth.
Put the ramen's dried vegetable packet in first.

examples.ko: 아이가 국의 건더기를 안 먹으려고 해요.
examples.en: My child doesn't want to eat the solids in the soup.
There's more broth than solids in this stew.
The broth is clear and there are plenty of solids too.

explain: 국이나 찌개에서 국물이 아니라 건져 먹는 고기, 채소, 두부 같은 재료를 말해요. 반대는 '국물'이에요. 라면 봉지에 있는 '건더기 수프'가 가장 쉬운 예예요.

phrases.en: There is nothing to find fault with in him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국 속 재료가 아니라 말이나 비판을 할 만한 구실, 거리라는 뜻으로 쓰여요. '트집 잡을 건더기', '말할 건더기'처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is not about soup ingredients but about grounds or material for criticism or talk. It appears in phrases like '트집 잡을 건더기'.
phrases.en_equiv: nothing to go on; no grounds

explain_en: In soups and stews it means the meat, vegetables or tofu that you scoop out and eat, as opposed to the broth. The opposite is '국물'. The '건더기 수프' packet in instant ramen is the easiest example.

en: to be thick; to be heavy; to be rich

examples.ko: 이 죽은 너무 걸쭉해서 숟가락이 안 움직여요.
examples.en: This porridge is so thick that the spoon won't move.

examples.ko: 국물이 걸쭉하게 될 때까지 천천히 끓여 주세요.
examples.en: Please simmer it slowly until the broth thickens.

examples.ko: 저는 묽은 수프보다 걸쭉한 수프를 더 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like thick soup more than watery soup.
You can turn off the heat once the sauce gets thick.
The curry I made yesterday was thicker than I expected.

examples.ko: 국물이 너무 걸쭉하지 않아서 먹기 편해요.
examples.en: The broth isn't too thick, so it's easy to eat.

explain: '진하다'는 맛이나 색이 짙다는 느낌이고, '걸쭉하다'는 액체가 묽지 않고 되직한 정도를 말해요. 죽, 수프, 소스를 설명할 때 자주 쓰고 반대말은 '묽다'예요.

phrases.en: Mom made me some thick porridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the form used to describe a noun that follows.

phrases.en: This soup is very thick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장을 끝낼 때 쓰는 해요체 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the polite -yo form for ending a sentence.

phrases.en: The sauce isn't thick, so it tastes bland.
phrases.nuance_ko: 묽은 상태를 말할 때 '묽다' 대신 부정형으로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can use the negative form to describe a thin liquid instead of saying 묽다.

explain_en: '진하다' is about strong flavor or deep color, while '걸쭉하다' is about a liquid being thick instead of watery. It is often used for porridge, soup and sauce, and the opposite is '묽다'.

examples.en: Seasoned bracken goes into bibimbap.
We pick bracken in the mountains in spring.
I boiled the bracken and left it soaking in water.
My grandmother sent me dried bracken.
Bracken is growing fast in the forest.
Seasoned bracken goes on the ancestral rites table.

explain: 한국에서는 말린 고사리를 물에 불려 삶아서 나물로 먹어요. 비빔밥과 육개장에 자주 들어가요. 반찬 이름으로는 '고사리나물'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: tiny little hands (of a child)
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이의 작고 통통한 손을 귀엽게 말할 때 써요. 어른의 손에는 쓰지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used affectionately for a child's small, chubby hands. Not used for adult hands.

explain_en: In Korea, dried bracken is soaked in water, boiled and eaten as a seasoned vegetable side dish. It often goes into bibimbap and 육개장. As a side dish, it is called '고사리나물'.

en: to be sweetish; to be somewhat sweet

examples.en: This sweet potato is pleasantly sweet, so it's good as a snack.
A mildly sweet taste lingered in my mouth.
The sikhye is nicely sweet and tasty.
Jujube tea is gently sweet and has a nice aroma.
Please make the sauce a little sweet.
The syrup is slightly sweet but not greasy.

explain: '달콤하다'보다 살짝, 은근하게 단 맛에 어울려요. 비슷한 말로 '달짝지근하다'도 있어요.

phrases.en: This tea has a slightly sweet taste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 활용형으로 맛을 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, often used to describe a taste.

phrases.en: This bread is slightly sweet, so it's tasty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달착지근하다와 뜻이 같은 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A variant with the same meaning as 달착지근하다.

phrases.en: The strawberries are sweet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달착지근하다보다 단맛이 분명하고 진한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sweeter and more distinct than 달착지근하다.

explain_en: Compared with '달콤하다', it fits a taste that is slightly or subtly sweet. '달짝지근하다' is a similar word.

examples.ko: 이 음료는 당류가 너무 많아서 자주 못 마셔요.
examples.en: This drink has too much sugar, so I can't drink it often.
The sugar content is written on the package.

examples.ko: 당류를 줄이려고 요즘 단 음료를 안 마셔요.
examples.en: I've stopped drinking sweet drinks lately to cut down on sugar.

examples.ko: 과일에 들어 있는 당류도 너무 많이 먹으면 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Even the sugars in fruit are not good if you eat too much.
I check the sugar on the nutrition label first.
I'm curious about the recommended daily amount of sugar.

explain: 영양 성분표나 식품 설명에서 보는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '설탕'이나 '단 것'이라고 많이 말해요. 당류에는 설탕뿐 아니라 포도당, 과당 같은 것도 들어가요.

phrases.en: I'm cutting down on sugars for my health.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건강이나 식단 이야기에서 '당류'와 가장 자주 함께 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for 당류 in talk about health and diet.

phrases.example: 과자를 살 때 당류 함량을 꼭 확인해요.
phrases.en: I always check the sugar content when I buy snacks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성분표에서 당류가 얼마나 들어 있는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for how much sugar a food contains, as on nutrition labels.

phrases.en: Please put just a little sugar in my coffee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '당류' 대신 '설탕'이나 '단 것'이라고 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk people say 설탕 or '단 것' instead of 당류.

explain_en: You see it on nutrition labels and food explanations. In daily talk people say '설탕' or '단 것'. The category covers not only table sugar but also things like glucose and fructose.

examples.en: For dinner today we grilled and ate sea bream.
The sea bream is fresh, so it's popular at the raw fish restaurant.
I bought one sea bream at the market.
Sea bream has soft flesh and a clean taste.
My father caught sea bream while fishing.
Steamed sea bream often shows up on feast tables.

explain: '도미'는 몸이 납작하고 붉은빛이 도는 바닷물고기예요. 한국에서는 회나 구이, 찜으로 먹고 잔칫날에 올리는 고급 생선이에요. 생선 이름 뒤에 '회', '구이', '찜'을 붙여서 '도미회', '도미찜'처럼 요리 이름을 만들어요.

phrases.en: We ordered sea bream sashimi at the raw fish restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도미를 날로 얇게 썬 음식이에요. '도미'만 말하면 생선 자체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the sliced raw dish; 도미 alone means the fish itself.

phrases.en: My mother made steamed sea bream for the holiday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도미를 쪄서 만든 요리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the dish made by steaming the fish.

phrases.en: I squeezed lemon over the grilled sea bream and ate it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도미를 불에 구운 요리예요. 집에서도 자주 해 먹어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The grilled dish; it is often made at home too.

explain_en: 도미 is a flat, reddish-tinted sea fish. In Korea it is eaten as raw fish, grilled, or steamed, and it is a high-quality fish served on feast days. Adding 회, 구이, or 찜 gives dish names like 도미회 and 도미찜.

examples.en: In winter I want to eat frozen pollack stew.
I bought two frozen pollack at the market.
Mom put the frozen pollack in the fridge.
We often eat pollack jeon on holidays.
This restaurant's pollack soup is delicious.
You have to thaw frozen pollack first.

explain: 명태는 상태에 따라 이름이 달라져요. 얼린 것은 동태, 말린 것은 북어, 반쯤 말린 것은 코다리예요. 동태는 주로 찌개나 전으로 먹어요.

phrases.en: Frozen pollack stew is tasty on cold days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동태로 끓인 대표적인 한국 음식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical Korean dish made with frozen pollack.

phrases.en: We pan-fry pollack jeon on holidays.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동태를 얇게 썰어 부친 전이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Thin slices of pollack battered and pan-fried.

phrases.en: How much is one frozen pollack?
phrases.nuance_ko: 생선을 셀 때는 '마리'를 써요. 시장에서 살 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fish are counted with 마리; common when shopping at a market.

explain_en: Pollack changes its name depending on its state: frozen is 동태, dried is 북어, and half-dried is 코다리. 동태 is mostly eaten in stew (동태찌개) or as jeon (동태전).

examples.ko: 만두소는 고기와 두부, 김치를 섞어서 만들어요.
examples.en: The dumpling filling is made by mixing meat, tofu and kimchi.

examples.ko: 만두소를 너무 많이 넣으면 만두가 터져요.
examples.en: If you put in too much filling, the dumplings burst.
Mom told me to taste the filling for seasoning.

examples.ko: 이 만두소는 부추가 들어가서 향이 좋아요.
examples.en: This filling has chives in it, so it smells good.
We made pan-fried patties with the leftover filling.
Please squeeze the moisture out of the filling well.

explain: '만두 속'이라고도 말해요. 같이 알아 두면 좋은 짝말은 '만두피'이고, 요리할 때 '소를 넣다', '소를 만들다'처럼 '소'만 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I put a lot of kimchi in the dumpling filling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만두소'를 띄어서 풀어 쓴 말로 뜻이 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same meaning as 만두소, written as two words.

phrases.en: Put the filling in the wrapper and fold it in half.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리 순서를 말할 때 '만두' 없이 '소'만 써도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: In recipes you can say just '소' without '만두'.

phrases.en: First, make the dumpling filling with tofu and meat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만두를 빚기 전에 속을 준비한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means preparing the filling before making the dumplings.

explain_en: People also say '만두 속'. A useful paired word is '만두피' (the wrapper), and when cooking you may hear just '소', as in '소를 넣다' (put in the filling).

examples.en: You have to knead the dough for a long time for the noodles to get chewy.

examples.ko: 이 집은 면발이 가늘어서 국물이 잘 배요.
examples.en: The noodles here are thin, so they soak up the broth well.
The noodles got too soggy, so they don't taste good.
For cold noodles, buckwheat noodles are the best.
I twirl a big bunch of noodles around my chopsticks and eat them.

examples.ko: 우동은 면발이 굵을수록 씹는 맛이 좋아요.
examples.en: The thicker the udon noodles are, the better they are to chew.

explain: 국수, 라면, 우동처럼 면 한 가닥 한 가닥의 식감을 말할 때 써요. '쫄깃하다', '탱탱하다', '불다'와 자주 함께 나와요. 음식 종류를 말할 때는 '면'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The udon at this place has chewy noodles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 면의 식감을 칭찬할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for praising noodle texture.

phrases.en: If you don't eat quickly, the noodles will get soggy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모음 앞에서는 'ㄷ 불규칙'이라 '면발이 불어요'로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a vowel it is a ㄷ irregular, so it becomes 'myeonbari bureoyo'.

phrases.en: If you eat it right after boiling, the noodles are springy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 면이 탄력 있고 단단하게 살아 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the noodles are firm and springy.

explain_en: Use it when you talk about the texture of the individual strands in noodle dishes such as guksu, ramyeon and udon. It often appears with '쫄깃하다' (chewy), '탱탱하다' (springy) and '불다' (get soggy). When you talk about the kind of food, people just say '면'.

en: to be thin; to be watery

examples.ko: 죽이 너무 묽어서 쌀을 더 넣었어요.
examples.en: The porridge was too thin, so I added more rice.

examples.ko: 묽은 수프는 빵에 찍어 먹기 어려워요.
examples.en: Thin soup is hard to eat by dipping bread in it.

examples.ko: 물감이 너무 묽으면 가루를 조금 더 섞으세요.
examples.en: If the paint is too thin, mix in a little more powder.

examples.ko: 반죽이 묽지 않게 밀가루를 조금 더 넣어요.
examples.en: Add a bit more flour so the batter isn't runny.
This yogurt is thinner than I expected.
The paint went on thin, so the color is pale.

explain: 국물, 죽, 반죽, 물감처럼 농도가 진하지 않고 물기가 많을 때 써요. '싱겁다'는 맛이 약한 거고 '묽다'는 걸쭉한 정도라서 달라요. 반대말은 '되다'나 '진하다'예요.

phrases.en: I added more flour to the thin batter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-은'을 붙여 명사를 꾸미는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-은' form modifies a noun.

phrases.en: This juice is watery because it has a lot of water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 서술형으로 맛이나 농도를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite ending, used to describe thickness or taste.

phrases.en: I added water to make the sauce thinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 일부러 묽게 한다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-게' shows that you make it thin on purpose.

explain_en: It describes soup, porridge, batter or paint that is not thick and has a lot of liquid. '싱겁다' is about weak flavor, while '묽다' is about thickness, so they differ. Its opposites are '되다' and '진하다'.

examples.ko: 이 수족관에서는 민물고기와 바다 어류를 한곳에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: At this aquarium you can see freshwater fish and sea fish in one place.
I made spicy fish stew with freshwater fish caught in the river.
Freshwater fish can't live long in seawater.
My father went out at dawn to catch freshwater fish.
Many freshwater fish live in this river.
That restaurant cooks freshwater fish dishes well.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '바닷물고기'예요. 강이나 호수에 사는 물고기를 말하고, 음식 이야기에서는 매운탕 재료로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: On the weekend I went to eat freshwater fish spicy stew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 이야기에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in talk about food.

phrases.en: My father caught freshwater fish in the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낚시나 그물로 물고기를 잡는 이야기에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about fishing or catching fish with a net.

phrases.en: Saltwater fish live in saltier water than freshwater fish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 민물고기와 짝이 되는 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart to 민물고기.

explain_en: Its counterpart is '바닷물고기' (saltwater fish). It means fish living in rivers and lakes, and in food talk it often comes up as an ingredient for 매운탕 (spicy fish stew).

examples.en: This morning I ate a bagel with cream cheese.
The bagels at this shop are chewy and delicious.

examples.ko: 베이글 두 개와 커피 한 잔 주세요.
examples.en: Two bagels and a cup of coffee, please.
These days, a bagel shop has opened in every neighborhood.
I toasted a bagel and made a sandwich.

examples.ko: 베이글은 크기가 커서 하나만 먹어도 든든해요.
examples.en: Bagels are big, so even one is filling.

explain: 영어 bagel을 그대로 가져온 외래어예요. 식빵은 부드럽지만 베이글은 '쫄깃하다'로 식감을 표현해요. '크림치즈 베이글', '베이글 샌드위치'처럼 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I had a cream cheese bagel for breakfast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카페에서 가장 흔한 조합이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common combination at cafés.

phrases.en: I bought a bagel sandwich for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 베이글 사이에 재료를 넣은 음식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A dish with fillings between bagel halves.

phrases.en: I baked bagels at home on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빵을 만들거나 오븐에 데울 때 '굽다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 굽다 is used for baking bread or heating it in the oven.

explain_en: 베이글 is a loanword taken straight from English bagel. Plain sandwich bread is soft, but a bagel's texture is described as 쫄깃하다 (chewy). Common combinations are 크림치즈 베이글 and 베이글 샌드위치.

examples.ko: 김치를 땅속에서 삭혀서 깊은 맛을 냈어요.
examples.en: I fermented the kimchi underground to get a deep flavor.
Skate is famous as a food eaten fermented.

examples.ko: 젓갈을 오래 삭히면 맛이 더 진해져요.
examples.en: If you ferment salted seafood for a long time, the flavor gets stronger.
Grandma ferments salted shrimp every year.

examples.ko: 잘 삭힌 장아찌는 밥에 올려 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: Well-fermented pickles are delicious on top of rice.

examples.ko: 삭히지 않고 바로 먹으면 맛이 많이 달라요.
examples.en: If you eat it right away without fermenting, the taste is very different.

explain: 김치, 젓갈, 홍어처럼 음식을 발효시켜 맛이 들게 할 때 써요. 음식이 저절로 익는 것은 '삭다'라고 해요. 화를 가라앉힐 때는 '삭히다'가 아니라 '삭이다'가 맞는 말이라 '화를 삭이다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Fermented skate has a very strong smell.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삭히다'를 꾸미는 말로 바꾼 형태로 음식 이름 앞에 자주 붙어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of 삭히다, often placed before a food name.

phrases.example: 새우젓은 몇 달 동안 삭혀서 만들어요.
phrases.en: Salted shrimp is made by fermenting it for several months.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 오래 두어 맛이 들게 하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes leaving food for a long time so its flavor develops.

phrases.en: The kimchi has fermented well and tastes good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 하는 일이 아니라 음식이 저절로 익는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes food ripening by itself rather than something a person does.

explain_en: It is used when you ferment food such as kimchi, salted seafood or skate until it ripens. When food ripens on its own, the verb is '삭다'. When calming anger, the correct word is '삭이다', not '삭히다', so say '화를 삭이다'.

examples.en: In autumn I go to the market to buy pomegranates.
Pomegranate juice is sweet and sour and tasty.
There is a pomegranate tree in the yard, so I picked the fruit.

examples.ko: 석류가 터지면 안에 빨간 알이 보여요.
examples.en: When a pomegranate splits, you can see red seeds inside.

examples.ko: 어머니가 석류를 한 알씩 까 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother peeled the pomegranate and gave it to me seed by seed.

examples.ko: 석류 껍질을 벗기는 게 조금 어려워요.
examples.en: Peeling a pomegranate is a bit difficult.

explain: 석류는 단단한 껍질 안에 빨갛고 작은 알이 가득한 과일이에요. 한국에서는 새콤한 맛과 건강 이미지 때문에 주스나 차로도 많이 마셔요. 나무는 '석류나무'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 아침에 석류 주스를 한 잔 마셨어요.
phrases.en: I drank a glass of pomegranate juice this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 석류로 만든 음료를 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, used for a drink made from pomegranates.

phrases.en: There is a pomegranate tree in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열매가 아니라 석류가 열리는 나무를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the tree that bears pomegranates, not the fruit itself.

phrases.en: I took out the pomegranate seeds one by one and ate them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 껍질 안의 빨갛고 작은 알을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the small red seeds inside the skin.

explain_en: 석류 is a fruit with a hard skin and many small red seeds inside. In Korea it is also drunk a lot as juice or tea, thanks to its tart taste and healthy image. The tree is called 석류나무.

examples.ko: 오후 세 시쯤 되니 시장기가 돌아요.
examples.en: Around three in the afternoon, I start to feel a little hungry.
I ate a piece of bread to take the edge off my hunger.

examples.ko: 시장기 때문에 수업에 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: I can't focus in class because I'm hungry.

examples.ko: 시장기도 없는데 친구가 먹자고 해서 먹었어요.
examples.en: I wasn't even hungry, but my friend wanted to eat, so I ate.

examples.ko: 시장기는 약간 느껴지는데 아직 밥때는 아니에요.
examples.en: I feel a bit hungry, but it's not mealtime yet.
Gimbap eaten when you're hungry tastes really good.

explain: '배고프다'보다 약하게, 슬슬 출출한 느낌을 말해요. '시장기가 돌다', '시장기를 달래다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 '출출하다'가 있어요.

phrases.example: 오후 세 시쯤 되니 시장기가 돌아요.
phrases.en: Around three in the afternoon, I start to feel a little hungry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 슬슬 출출해지기 시작할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 꼴이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for when you start to feel a bit peckish.

phrases.en: I ate a piece of bread to tide over my hunger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간단히 먹어서 배고픔을 조금 가라앉힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when eating something small to take the edge off hunger.

phrases.en: I'm a little hungry; shall we have a snack?
phrases.nuance_ko: '시장기'와 비슷하게 약한 배고픔을 나타내는 형용사로 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adjective for mild hunger similar to 시장기, used more often in daily conversation.

explain_en: It describes a milder, peckish kind of hunger than '배고프다'. It is used in '시장기가 돌다' and '시장기를 달래다'. A similar word is '출출하다'.

en: to be slightly bitter; to be bitterish

examples.en: This tea tastes a little bitter.
A slightly bitter coffee is perfect in the morning.
I like dark chocolate because it is pleasantly bitter.

examples.ko: 쌉쌀한 맛 때문에 아이들은 안 먹어요.
examples.en: Kids don't eat it because of the bitter taste.
It is bitter at first, but sweet afterward.

examples.ko: 녹차를 너무 쌉쌀하지 않게 우려 주세요.
examples.en: Please brew the green tea so it isn't too bitter.

explain: '쓰다'보다 약하고, 싫지 않은 쓴맛이라는 느낌으로 써요. 커피, 차, 초콜릿, 나물 같은 음식 맛을 말할 때 잘 나와요. 칭찬하는 말투로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The slightly bitter taste is the charm of this chocolate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식의 맛을 칭찬하면서 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to describe a flavor in a positive way.

phrases.en: This tea is not bitter and is smooth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓴맛이 거의 없다고 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says there is hardly any bitterness.

phrases.en: Mugwort tea is a little bitterish.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쌉쌀하다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word with almost the same meaning as '쌉쌀하다'.

explain_en: It is milder than '쓰다' and suggests a bitterness that is not unpleasant. It often describes coffee, tea, chocolate and wild greens. People often use it in a positive tone.

examples.ko: 여름에는 시원한 오이소박이가 입맛을 살려 줘요.
examples.en: In summer, cool stuffed cucumber kimchi brings back your appetite.
My mother is making stuffed cucumber kimchi.
Stuffed cucumber kimchi is made with a chive seasoning filling.
It's really tasty to have stuffed cucumber kimchi with noodles.
Stuffed cucumber kimchi came out as a side dish at the restaurant.

examples.ko: 오이소박이는 오래 두면 물러져서 빨리 먹어야 해요.
examples.en: Stuffed cucumber kimchi gets soft if left long, so you should eat it soon.

explain: 오이에 칼집을 내고 양념 속을 채워 만든 여름 김치예요. 일반 김치보다 오래 두기 어려워서 보통 담근 뒤 며칠 안에 먹어요. 줄여서 '소박이'라고 하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I bought a little oisobagi at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오이소박이'를 줄여 편하게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened, casual way to say 오이소박이.

phrases.en: I eat oisobagi alongside ramyeon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 음식과 함께 먹는다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means eating it together with another dish.
phrases.en_equiv: to have oisobagi on the side

phrases.en: The filling for oisobagi is made with chives.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오이 안에 넣는 양념을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the seasoned stuffing put inside the cucumber.

explain_en: It is a summer kimchi made by slitting a cucumber and stuffing it with seasoning. It does not keep as long as regular kimchi, so people usually eat it within a few days. It is sometimes shortened to '소박이'.

examples.en: Drinking yuzu tea in winter warms the body.
The yuzu scent is subtle, and it puts me in a good mood.
Mom made yuzu preserve for me.
A yuzu has a bumpier skin than a tangerine.

examples.ko: 목이 아플 때 유자 꿀물을 마셨어요.
examples.en: When my throat hurt, I drank yuzu honey water.

examples.ko: 유자 하나를 잘라서 향을 맡아 봤어요.
examples.en: I cut open a yuzu and smelled it.

explain: 유자는 향이 강하고 신맛이 있어서 과일로 바로 먹기보다 차나 '청'(설탕에 절인 것)으로 먹어요. '유자차'가 가장 흔해요. 귤과 달리 껍질까지 함께 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I had a cold, so I drank warm yuzu tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유자를 가장 흔하게 먹는 방법이고, 겨울에 많이 마셔요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to have yuzu, often drunk in winter.

phrases.example: 유자청에 뜨거운 물을 부으면 유자차가 돼요.
phrases.en: If you pour hot water on yuzu syrup, it becomes yuzu tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설탕에 절인 유자로, 물을 부어 차로 마셔요.
phrases.nuance_en: Yuzu preserved in sugar, used to make tea.

phrases.en: This candy is yuzu flavored.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과자나 음료의 맛을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the flavor of snacks or drinks.

explain_en: 유자 has a strong scent and a sour taste, so it is eaten as tea or as 청 (fruit preserved in sugar) rather than raw as a fruit. 유자차 is by far the most common form. Unlike a 귤 (tangerine), the peel is often used along with the fruit.

examples.ko: 건강을 위해 흰쌀 대신 잡곡을 먹어요.
examples.en: For my health, I eat mixed grains instead of white rice.
I looked around the mixed grains section at the mart.
Mixed grains are chewier than rice.

examples.ko: 보리와 콩 같은 잡곡이 밥에 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: Grains like barley and beans go well in rice.
This shop sells only domestically grown grains.
They say mixed grains have a lot of dietary fiber.

explain: 쌀을 뺀 보리, 콩, 수수, 조 같은 곡식을 한데 묶어 부르는 말이에요. 건강 이야기에서 '흰쌀'과 대비해서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I mix grains into the rice when I cook it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥 지을 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase when cooking rice.

phrases.example: 잡곡이 몸에 좋다고 해서 사 왔어요.
phrases.en: I bought some because they say mixed grains are good for you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건강 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in talk about health.

phrases.example: 이 빵에는 여러 가지 잡곡이 들어 있어요.
phrases.en: This bread contains several kinds of grains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식에 들어간 재료를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe what is in a food.

explain_en: It groups together grains other than rice, such as barley, beans, sorghum and millet. It often appears in health talk as a contrast to '흰쌀' (white rice).

examples.en: I only drink low-fat milk.
I'm losing weight with a low-fat diet.
This yogurt is low-fat but still tasty.

examples.ko: 저지방 제품이라고 해서 칼로리가 꼭 낮은 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Just because a product is low-fat doesn't mean it's low in calories.
I picked low-fat cheese at the supermarket.
Which should I buy, low-fat or fat-free?

explain: 주로 우유, 요거트, 치즈 같은 식품 앞에 붙여서 써요. 지방이 거의 없는 '무지방'과 구별해서 말해요. 저지방이 저칼로리와 같은 말은 아니에요.

phrases.en: I eat low-fat yogurt in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식품 이름 앞에 '저지방'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 저지방 before a food name.

phrases.en: I chose low-fat foods at the supermarket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지방이 적은 음식을 넓게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used broadly for foods low in fat.

phrases.en: This milk is fat-free, so it tastes light.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지방이 거의 없는 것으로 저지방보다 더 적어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has almost no fat, even less than 저지방.

explain_en: It is mostly attached to foods like milk, yogurt and cheese. It is distinguished from '무지방', which means almost no fat. Low-fat is not the same as low-calorie.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 반찬으로 무 절임이 나와요.
examples.en: This restaurant serves pickled radish as a side dish.
Pickled cucumbers are sour and crunchy.

examples.ko: 절임 음식은 너무 짜지 않게 먹어야 해요.
examples.en: Pickled food should be eaten in a way that isn't too salty.

examples.ko: 할머니가 직접 만든 절임을 선물로 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother gave me pickles she made herself as a gift.
There is some pickled garlic left in the fridge.

examples.ko: 절임에 쓰는 소금은 따로 사야 해요.
examples.en: You have to buy the salt used for pickling separately.

explain: '무 절임', '오이 절임'처럼 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 써요. 간장이나 된장에 담근 반찬은 '장아찌'라고 따로 불러요. 동사는 '절이다'이고, 김치도 배추를 절여서 만들지만 보통 절임이라고 하지 않아요.

phrases.example: 양파 절임은 새콤해서 고기와 잘 맞아요.
phrases.en: Pickled onions are sour and go well with meat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 쓰는 방법이에요. 다른 채소도 같은 식으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the pattern of putting the ingredient first. Other vegetables work the same way.

phrases.en: A pickled side dish came out for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반찬의 종류를 말할 때 써요. 식당 이야기에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name a kind of side dish. Often heard in talk about restaurants.

phrases.example: 절임 채소는 오래 두고 먹을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Pickled vegetables can be kept and eaten for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 절여서 만든 채소를 모두 말해요. 여러 종류를 한꺼번에 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Covers all vegetables made by pickling. Used when talking about many kinds at once.

explain_en: Put the ingredient first, as in '무 절임' (pickled radish) or '오이 절임'. Side dishes preserved in soy sauce or soybean paste have their own name, 장아찌. The verb is 절이다, and although kimchi is made by salting cabbage, it is not usually called 절임.

examples.en: I bought one geun of pork at the butcher shop.
The meat at this butcher shop is always fresh.
I picked out some beef at the meat section.

examples.ko: 마트 정육 코너는 저녁에 할인을 해요.
examples.en: The meat section at the mart has a discount in the evening.

examples.ko: 정육점 아저씨가 고기를 얇게 썰어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The butcher sliced the meat thinly for me.

examples.ko: 저는 주말마다 정육점에 들러 고기를 사요.
examples.en: I stop by the butcher shop every weekend to buy meat.

explain: 뼈와 기름을 발라낸 살코기를 뜻하지만, 실제로는 '정육점', '정육 코너'처럼 가게나 매장 이름으로 가장 많이 들어요. 고기를 사는 이야기에서는 '정육점에 가다'라고 말해요. 옛날식 표현으로 '푸줏간'도 있어요.

phrases.en: I went to the butcher shop to buy something for dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고기를 파는 가게를 뜻하며 '정육'이 가장 자주 쓰이는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a shop selling meat, and it's the most common form using 정육.

phrases.en: I bought beef at the meat section of the supermarket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마트에서 고기를 파는 자리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the meat area in a supermarket.

phrases.en: I heard that in the old days every neighborhood had a butcher's.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정육점'의 옛날식 말이라 요즘은 드물게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An old-fashioned word for 정육점, rarely used these days.

explain_en: It means meat with the bones and fat removed, but in practice you hear it most in shop names like '정육점' (butcher shop) and '정육 코너' (meat section). When talking about buying meat, people say '정육점에 가다'. An old-fashioned word for the same shop is '푸줏간'.

examples.en: The meat sizzles as it cooks on the grill.

examples.ko: 지글지글 끓는 찌개를 먹었더니 땀이 났어요.
examples.en: I ate a bubbling-hot stew and started sweating.
It's midday with the sun beating down fiercely.
A sizzling sound is coming from the griddle.
I can hear the sizzle of pancakes frying.

examples.ko: 지글지글 구운 고기에 쌈을 싸 먹었어요.
examples.en: I wrapped the sizzling grilled meat in a leaf and ate it.

explain: 고기 굽는 소리처럼 '지글지글 익다/구워지다'로 써요. '지글지글 끓다'처럼 아주 뜨겁게 끓거나 햇볕이 뜨거운 느낌에도 써요. 동사는 '지글거리다'예요.

phrases.en: I can smell the pancake sizzling as it cooks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 구워지며 나는 소리를 말할 때 가장 기본으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic use, for the sound of food cooking.

phrases.en: The heated floor is piping hot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닥이나 국물이 아주 뜨거운 느낌을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Conveys a floor or soup being extremely hot.

phrases.en: The midsummer sun is scorching down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 햇볕이 몹시 뜨거울 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the sun is extremely hot.

explain_en: It is used for sounds like meat grilling, as in '지글지글 익다/구워지다'. It also conveys intense heat, as in '지글지글 끓다' or scorching sunshine. The verb form is '지글거리다'.

examples.en: On hot summer days I crave a cold soft drink.

examples.ko: 청량음료를 너무 많이 마시면 이에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Drinking too much soda is bad for your teeth.
I bought popcorn and a soft drink at the cinema.
I like water better than soft drinks.
I got a can of soda from the vending machine.

examples.ko: 청량음료 대신 차를 마시는 건 어때요?
examples.en: How about drinking tea instead of soda?

explain: 콜라나 사이다처럼 시원하고 달콤한 음료를 두루 부르는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '탄산음료'나 '콜라, 사이다'처럼 말하는 때가 많고, '청량음료'는 설명이나 상품 소개에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I drink water more often than soda.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 청량음료 대신 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word used more often in everyday talk instead of 청량음료.

phrases.en: Drinking a soft drink after exercise is refreshing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음료를 마신다는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic verb pairing for drinking one.

phrases.en: I order cola or lemon-lime soda at restaurants.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청량음료의 대표 예를 직접 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names typical examples of soft drinks directly.

explain_en: It is a general term for cool, sweet drinks like cola and cider (soda). In daily talk people often say '탄산음료' or name the drink, like '콜라' or '사이다', while '청량음료' shows up more in explanations and product descriptions.

examples.en: I knead the dough by hand for a long time.

examples.ko: 빵을 만들 때 반죽을 힘껏 치댔어요.
examples.en: When making bread, I kneaded the dough with all my strength.

examples.ko: 쫄깃한 수제비를 만들려면 반죽을 많이 치대야 해요.
examples.en: To make chewy sujebi, you have to knead the dough a lot.
I knead the clay to make it soft.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마한테 치대며 놀아 달라고 해요.
examples.en: The child clings to Mom, asking her to play.

examples.ko: 동생이 자꾸 치대서 숙제를 못 했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling kept pestering me, so I couldn't do my homework.

explain: '주무르다'보다 손바닥이나 팔에 힘을 주어 눌러 가며 문지르는 느낌이에요. 빵, 수제비, 칼국수 반죽을 만들 때 많이 써요. 또 사람에게 자꾸 달라붙어 귀찮게 구는 모습에도 쓰는데, 이때는 편한 사이의 대화에서 써요.

phrases.en: If you knead the sujebi dough well, it becomes chewy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반죽을 힘주어 누르며 문지를 때 쓰는 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The typical collocation for pressing and working dough with force.

phrases.example: 동생이 자꾸 치대서 숙제를 못 해요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling keeps clinging to me, so I can't do my homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람에게 달라붙어 귀찮게 구는 뜻으로 편한 사이에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to cling and pester someone; used casually among close people.

phrases.en: Please work the dough with your hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: '치대다'보다 힘을 덜 주고 부드럽게 만지는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels gentler than 'chidaeda', using less force.

explain_en: Compared with '주무르다', it has the feel of pressing and rubbing with the palm or arm putting in some force. It is often used for making dough for bread, sujebi and kalguksu. It is also used for someone who keeps clinging to and bothering a person, and in that sense it is for casual conversation.

en: to eat only what one wants

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 채소를 안 먹고 편식해요.
examples.en: My child doesn't eat vegetables and is a picky eater.

examples.ko: 편식하면 키가 안 클 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you're a picky eater, you may not grow tall.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 편식했는데 지금은 다 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: I was a picky eater as a child, but now I eat everything.
I'm trying to fix my habit of picky eating.

examples.ko: 급식 시간에 아이들이 편식하지 않도록 선생님이 도와줘요.
examples.en: At lunch time, the teacher helps the children not to eat only what they like.
After being a picky eater for a long time, my body got weaker.

explain: 좋아하는 음식만 먹고 다른 음식은 안 먹는 습관이에요. 아이에게는 '편식하지 마'라고 자주 말하고, 같은 뜻의 '가리다'는 '음식을 가리다'로 써요. 반대로 뭐든 잘 먹는 사람은 '골고루 먹다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 저는 편식하지 않고 다 잘 먹어요.
phrases.en: I'm not a picky eater and eat everything well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 가리지 않고 먹는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you eat without being picky.
phrases.en_equiv: not to be a picky eater

phrases.en: I'm worried because my child is picky about food.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편식하다'와 같은 뜻이고, 일상 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 편식하다, and common in daily talk.

phrases.en: You should eat a bit of everything, including vegetables.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편식하다'의 반대로, 여러 음식을 다 먹는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 편식하다: eating a variety of foods.

explain_en: 편식하다 describes eating only favorite foods. Parents often say 편식하지 마 to children; the verb 가리다 works in 음식을 가리다 for the same idea. The opposite habit is expressed with 골고루 먹다.

examples.en: A lot of seaweed washed up on the beach.
I like seaweed salad.
The fish are hiding among the seaweed.

examples.ko: 해초를 말려서 차로 마시는 곳도 있어요.
examples.en: Some places dry seaweed and drink it as tea.
Seaweed wrapped around my foot and it startled me.
It tastes good because it grew in clean seawater.

explain: 먹는 바다 식물은 보통 '미역', '김', '다시마'처럼 이름을 따로 불러요. 해초는 바다 식물 전체를 묶어서 말할 때 써요. 그래서 식당에서는 '해초 샐러드'처럼 메뉴 이름에서 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: This restaurant is famous for its seaweed dishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해초로 만든 음식을 두루 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for any food made from sea plants.

phrases.en: People in Japan often eat seaweed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹는 대상으로 말할 때 '해초를'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '해초를' when it is the thing being eaten.

phrases.en: Haecho are plants that grow in the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해초'를 쉬운 말로 풀어서 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain way to explain what '해초' means.

explain_en: Edible sea plants usually go by their own names such as '미역', '김' and '다시마'. 해초 groups all of them together. You often see it in menu names like '해초 샐러드'.

en: flavor enhancer; artificial flavors; chemical condiment

examples.ko: 이 식당은 화학조미료를 안 쓴다고 쓰여 있어요.
examples.en: This restaurant says it doesn't use artificial flavor enhancers.

examples.ko: 어머니는 화학조미료 대신 멸치 육수를 쓰세요.
examples.en: My mother uses anchovy broth instead of chemical seasoning.
I want to avoid food with chemical seasoning in it.

examples.ko: 라면 스프에 화학조미료가 들어 있는지 봤어요.
examples.en: I checked whether the ramen seasoning packet contains artificial flavoring.
These days there are many products with no added chemical seasoning.

examples.ko: 화학조미료를 많이 넣은 국은 맛이 너무 진해요.
examples.en: Soup with a lot of chemical seasoning tastes too strong.

explain: 음식 이야기에서는 그냥 '조미료'라고도 많이 말해요. '무첨가', '안 쓴다'와 같이 쓰이는 경우가 많고, 반대쪽 느낌의 말은 '천연 조미료'예요.

phrases.en: I put only a little seasoning in this soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '화학조미료'를 줄여 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, 'hwahakjomiryo' is often shortened to this.

phrases.example: 저는 멸치로 만든 천연 조미료를 써요.
phrases.en: I use a natural seasoning made from anchovies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화학조미료와 반대되는 느낌의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite feel of chemical seasoning.

phrases.en: I heard that restaurant doesn't add chemical seasoning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '넣다/안 넣다'는 음식 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Add / not add' is a common pair in food talk.

explain_en: In food talk, people often just say '조미료'. It often appears with '무첨가' or '안 쓴다', and the opposite idea is '천연 조미료' (natural seasoning).
